note: Fourth western state off the federal gap list. 16 likely_rv rows, none already in the database by recreation.gov id. 10 added, 6 excluded, each with the kind of no. Forest Service sites on the Dixie, Fishlake, Manti-La Sal and Uinta-Wasatch-Cache, and BLM sites near Moab, Green River, Beaver and the Paria. One row RIDB files under UT (Echo Park) actually sits in Colorado and is excluded on access regardless.

added.name: Hanging Rock Campground (Beaver River)
added.caveat: no published site length and no per-site coordinates; a dated review (2024-07) got a 32-ft Class C in, entry 'somewhat tight'

added.name: Willow Lake Campground (Manti-La Sal NF)
added.caveat: only sites 1-3 permit RVs and trailers (30 ft); the rest are van/pickup-camper/pop-up

added.name: White House Campground (Paria River)
added.caveat: no published site length; 2 miles of washboard with two big dips; reviewers: a 21-ft trailer dragged its bumper (2019), a 26-ft RV got in (2020), one reviewer claims an 18-ft trailer maximum. Kept on the 2020 firsthand report; a judgement call

excluded.name: Westwater Campground (Ranger Station)
excluded.why: every one of the 11 catalog sites states Max Vehicle Length 17 ft and permits only cars, vans, pickup campers and tents - no RV or trailer on any site

excluded.name: Echo Park Campground (Dinosaur NM)
excluded.why: NPS: the Echo Park Road 'is not suitable for RVs'; high clearance and 4WD strongly recommended for the dugway switchbacks, impassable when wet. Also note the campground is in Colorado (Moffat County), not Utah as RIDB files it

excluded.name: MAPLE CANYON
excluded.why: recreation.gov notice: 'RVs and trailers are not recommended'; catalog sites 20 ft save one at 25 ft, narrow dirt canyon road

excluded.name: WOLF CREEK (UT)
excluded.why: the three single sites state 15 ft; the only longer sites are the two group sites (group-only for a 23-ft rig)

excluded.name: Stateline Campground Long Term
excluded.why: three sites of Stateline Campground (added as 13229) sold separately with a 30-night minimum; recorded in that entry's note rather than as a second entry

method_notes: No per-site water flag existed on Cedar Canyon, so its creekside call rests on the z18 imagery, where Crow Creek's channel is legible beside the south row, plus the OSM line 5-13 m from eight pads. Rosebud's single pad at 24 m from Pleasant Creek was NOT promoted: a riparian band stands between and nothing qualifying confirms it. Oak Creek's unnamed OSM stream (23-38 m under canopy, never mentioned by the agency) likewise stays down.
Two rows without per-site coordinates (Hanging Rock, White House) were placed from the facility pin and read at z18/z19; both pins sit on the campground.
Overpass's main endpoint 504'd repeatedly; the water measurements went through on retry.
